title: On-call checklist fabricator with trace-handoff to PagerDuty and Slack runbook sync
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a lightweight "fabricator" service that auto-generates a checklist message in the on-call Slack channel and attaches a structured trace handoff to PagerDuty incidents. The service will synthesize: (1) a minimal, actionable on-call checklist tailored from the runbook template for the alert class, (2) a single-click link to attach the top-K related traces and span snippets, and (3) an idempotent sync that ensures runbook edits in the Console are reflected within Slack checklist templates and the PagerDuty incident notes. Goals: reduce mean time to investigation (MTTI) for service-level latency spikes, standardize first-responder actions, and lower cognitive load during triage.
acceptance_criteria: Given a high-latency SLO alert, the fabricator creates a Slack checklist message in the designated on-call channel within 10s of alert firing with: incident id, severity, top-3 hypothesis steps from the runbook template, and links to the Console trace viewer.

When a PagerDuty incident is auto-created via the existing alerting rule, the PagerDuty incident includes a JSON attachment (or note) with a trace-handoff payload: top-3 trace IDs, truncated stack/span snippets, and a suggested rollback command if present in the runbook.

Runbook edits in the Console (title/body/steps) are visible in the next fabricator-generated checklist without manual refresh; diffs are stored and visible in the checklist footer with a link to the runbook edit history.

The fabricator supports manual re-run (from Slack message action) to reattach traces after additional telemetry arrives; repeated runs are idempotent and append a timestamped revision to the checklist thread.
All network calls to PagerDuty and Slack use retry with exponential backoff; failures are surfaced to a small ops channel and the incident is annotated in Console with failure markers.
End-to-end tests simulate alert -> fabricator -> slack + pd flows and assertions run in CI with mocked PD/Slack APIs. Coverage for error paths and idempotency behavior is included.
Security review completed and KMS key usage for any persisted sensitive context is documented in the PR and Confluence design doc.
comments: 2026-03-05 Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to keep fabricator as a thin service in infra namespace, reuse existing trace-selection heuristics (ENG-25673) and Console runbook storage. Decided PD attachment format should be a single note with a compact JSON and human summary.

2026-03-07 Marcus Chen: Spike complete. Implemented PoC that generates a Slack checklist message and posts a PD note with sample trace ids. PoC repo: github.com/redwood/ops-fabricator/poc. Observations: trace selection needs tie-breaker for similar latencies; will add weight by error rate and CPU spike correlation.

2026-03-09 Elena Park (Design): Reviewed checklist UX. Recommend grouping steps into 'Immediate' vs 'Investigate' to reduce action friction. Suggested adding a small 'confidence' indicator for each hypothesis derived from telemetry signals.

2026-03-11 Marcus Chen: Started integration tests. Using mocked PD and Slack endpoints from test harness. Found race where runbook edits during incident create inconsistent checklist content; implementing a runbook revision lock and optimistic merge.

2026-03-12 Security review required: flagged storage of span snippets. Added requirement to truncate and redact PII before any persistence; KMS key id: projects/redwood/kms/ops-fabricator (to be confirmed in infra onboarding).
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for checklist generation and trace selection heuristics. 2) Integration tests with mocked Slack/PagerDuty verifying idempotency, retries, and error annotations. 3) End-to-end staging deployment: wire to a non-prod alert rule and validate checklist + PD notes appear with redaction policy. 4) Load test to ensure fabricator handles 200 alerts/min with <200ms decision latency on average.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse trace scorer library from trace-selection service; add new weighting for 'time-since-alert' and 'error-count'.
- Use Slack block kit for checklist message with action buttons: 'Attach traces', 'Rerun fabricator', 'Mark acknowledged'.
- PD attachment via Events API v2 as a note; include compact JSON blob under 'ops_context' key.
- Store minimal incident-context in DynamoDB table (incident_id -> runbook_rev -> attachments) with TTL 7d. Truncate snippets to 2KB per span and run through redactor prior to storage.
- Metrics: fabricator.latency_ms, fabricator.post_slack_success, fabricator.post_pd_success, fabricator.retries.
- Access control: service account with least privilege; PD token and Slack bot token stored in secrets manager.
